title: The Drowned Salt
premise: Lior Oyelaran, the last of the oath-bound swordspeakers, has spent a decade hiding her gift—words that cut deeper than steel—in the smuggler's passes of the Thornfell mountains. When a dying courier presses a salt-stained map into her hands, she learns the drowned court beneath Mount Serein holds a stolen soul: her own, sold by the mother who bound her oaths, and the court's tide-priests mean to use it to wake something older than winter. Guided by a disgraced priest named Cassian and hunted by the Hollow Guard, Lior descends through the mountain's flooded halls to reclaim what was taken from her. In the end she must choose between destroying the soul and thus her own power forever, or binding it back at the cost of speaking one true word that will unmake the lies holding the mountain's court together—and exile her from every road she knows.
about_author: Elodie Joubert is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent five years mapping cave systems in the Pyrenees before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about borders, bargains, and the people who live in the gaps between them.

chapters.title: Salt on the Wind
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She guides a smuggling caravan through a snowbound pass, using just enough swordspeech to turn aside a rockslide, and hates herself for the small indulgence. Beat: establish her invisibility as both armor and prison; ends when she finds a stranger bleeding out on the high trail.

chapters.title: The Dying Courier
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The stranger, mouth full of seawater he couldn't possibly have swallowed, presses a map into her hands and whispers 'the ninth door remembers you' before dying. The Hollow Guard arrives minutes later. Beat: dread and reluctant responsibility as she escapes with the map.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Lior's POV in a safehouse tavern. The map depicts the drowned halls beneath Mount Serein, marked with her mother's handwriting and a route only an Oyelaran could walk. Beat: identity shaken—the past she fled has been waiting for her.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. A defrocked tide-priest recognizes the map's seal and hunts Lior down—not to take it, but to beg passage. He reveals the court is harvesting souls to feed something called the Long Tide. Beat: uneasy alliance born of mutual desperation.

chapters.title: Hollow Riders
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Hollow Guard ambushes them at a river ford; Lior breaks her silence with a spoken cutting-word that kills three riders, and Cassian sees what she truly is. Beat: power's cost made visible—her words leave frost-scars on her tongue.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. They seek refuge with Vess, Lior's old fence, who demands a price: the map's copy rights and a truth about why the Guard tracks Lior specifically. Beat: loyalty tested against self-interest; Vess chooses friendship over profit, barely.

chapters.title: Ninth Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They reach the mountain's hidden entrance, which opens only to swordspeech—proof someone expected an Oyelaran. Inside, stairs descend into warm black water. Beat: point of no return; fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Disguised as pilgrims, they witness the drowned court: nobles breathing water, tide-priests auctioning bottled souls. Cassian recognizes his former mentor among them. Beat: wonder curdling into horror; corruption wears beautiful faces.

chapters.title: A Name in a Bottle
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the vault of souls she finds a bottle bearing her own name—and hears it whisper in her mother's voice. She steals it, tripping an alarm of singing brine. Beat: identity crisis peaks; is the soul hers, or a lure?

chapters.title: The Hunted Corridors
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A chase through flooded galleries as the Hollow Guard and court wardens converge. Cassian is captured buying time. Beat: guilt and fury drive Lior deeper instead of out.

chapters.title: The Tide-Priest's Offer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. High Priestess Maren corners her, not with force but with a bargain: surrender the bottle and receive her mother, alive, held in the deep. Beat: temptation framed as mercy; loyalty vs. truth collide.

chapters.title: Prisoner of Salt
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. In the cells, Cassian endures interrogation by his mentor, who offers restoration of his rank if he betrays Lior's route. He refuses—but we learn he once sold a secret before. Beat: redemption must be earned twice.

chapters.title: The Mother's Confession
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior trades the bottle for a meeting with her mother, who confesses she sold Lior's soul to save her from a prophecy naming her the Long Tide's vessel. Beat: devastating truth—protection and betrayal were the same act.

chapters.title: Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Above, the first true blizzard seals the passes; below, the court begins the Rite of the Long Tide early. Escape routes close one by one. Beat: ticking clock made physical; despair before defiance.

chapters.title: Breaking the Bottle
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Alone, Lior nearly shatters the soul-bottle to deny the court its prize, but the whispering soul shows her memories she never lived—a whole self waiting. Beat: darkest hour; she cannot destroy what she doesn't yet understand.

chapters.title: Vess Comes Down the Mountain
chapters.summary: Vess's POV (first appearance). Refusing to abandon Lior, Vess leads smugglers through a collapsed pass to breach the ninth door behind the Guard. Beat: loyalty answered; hope arrives battered and armed.

chapters.title: The Rite of the Long Tide
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The court begins the rite; Maren pours harvested souls into the sleeping thing beneath the mountain, which stirs. Lior interrupts, sword-words blazing, and frees Cassian mid-ceremony. Beat: open battle; power wielded openly at last.

chapters.title: One True Word
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian realizes the Long Tide is fed by lies—it exists because the court's founding bargain was built on a false oath. Only a swordspeaker's true word can unmake it. Beat: the plan crystallizes; terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Drowned Throne
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax part one: Lior fights her way to the throne as the mountain floods, her mother sacrificing herself to hold the Guard back. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; forgiveness given too late to be easy.

chapters.title: Swordspeech
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax part two: Lior binds her soul back into herself and speaks one absolute true word—that the bargain was never kept—which unmakes the Long Tide and dissolves the court's power. Beat: triumph inseparable from loss; her gift burns out.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. The survivors surface into deep snow; the freed souls disperse like light. Cassian chooses to stay and rebuild rather than return to his old life. Beat: quiet aftermath; wounds acknowledged, not erased.

chapters.title: Every Road She Knows
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Powerless but whole, Lior walks out of the Thornfell with Vess, no longer hiding—there is nothing left in her to hunt. She takes the map's blank reverse and begins drawing new roads. Beat: resolution; identity rebuilt on choice rather than oath.
